title: Stripe SDK Update Broke iOS Checkout
description: A deployment updating the Stripe SDK on the iOS checkout module introduced a critical failure in the payment flow, causing a 65% drop in iOS revenue. The PR was merged 2 hours before the anomaly started and directly modified the iOS checkout payment module.

evidence_matrix.details: GitHub PR merged exactly 2 hours before anomaly start, modifying iOS checkout payment module.
iOS checkout error rate jumped from 0.3% to 42% immediately after the deployment window.
Anomaly decomposition identifies iOS as the primary driver with 87% contribution to the aggregate revenue drop.
Revenue on iOS recovered to baseline within 2 hours of the Stripe SDK rollback deployment.

title: Push Notification Bug Caused App Uninstalls
description: A misconfigured push notification campaign sent excessive alerts to iOS users, leading to a spike in app uninstalls and reduced active user count during the anomaly window.

evidence_matrix.details: Push notification config change timestamp is ambiguous; may have preceded or coincided with anomaly.
No checkout error rate spike observed from push notifications; the failure mode is user churn, not transaction errors.
Push notification bug affected iOS users, matching the primary driver segment.
App Store uninstall rate was 3.2x baseline during the anomaly window for the iOS segment.

title: Seasonal Traffic Decline
description: Normal seasonal traffic patterns may explain part of the revenue dip, as mid-June historically shows lower conversion rates.

evidence_matrix.details: No deployment or operational event corresponds to this hypothesis.
Year-over-year comparison shows a 5-8% dip in mid-June, but the current 65% drop far exceeds historical variance.
Seasonal patterns affect all segments uniformly; they do not explain iOS-specific concentration.
